'''Caius Iacob''' (March 29, 1912 – February 6, 1992) was a [[Romania]]n mathematician, professor at the [[University of Bucharest]], and titular member of the [[Romanian Academy]]. After the [[Romanian Revolution|fall of communism]] in  1989, he was elected to the [[Senate of Romania]].

==Biography==
He was born in [[Arad, Romania|Arad]], the son of {{ill|Lazăr Iacob|ro|Iacob Lazăr}} and Camelia, née Moldovan. His father was professor of Canon Law, and served as delegate for Arad at the [[Great National Assembly of Alba Iulia]] of 1 December 1918.<ref name="AC">{{citation|author=Adrian Corduneanu |url=http://www.recreatiimatematice.ro/arhiva/istoria/RM22012IACOB.pdf|title=Caius Iacob – 100 de ani de la naștere|journal=Recreații Matematice| language=ro|year=2012|issue=1|pages=87–88}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dacoromania-alba.ro/nr67/gazeta.htm|title=Membrii de drept ai Marii Adunării Naționale de la Alba-Iulia din 1 decembrie 1918|language=ro|publisher=Gazeta Oficială|location=Sibiu|volume= 1|date=14 December 1918|website=www.dacoromania-alba.ro|access-date=30 December 2021}}</ref> Caius Iacob attended the [[Moise Nicoară National College|Moise Nicoară High School]] in his native city, and then completed his secondary education at the [[Emanuil Gojdu National College|Emanuil Gojdu High School]] in [[Oradea]]. After passing his [[Bachelor's degree|baccalaureate examination]] with the highest mark in the nation, he was admitted in 1928 at the Faculty of Sciences of the [[University of Bucharest]], from where he graduated in 1931, aged nineteen.<ref name="AC"/><ref name="Mac"/> Iacob continued his studies at the Faculty of Sciences of the [[University of Paris]], with thesis advisor [[Henri Villat]]. He defended his thesis, ''Sur la détermination des fonctions harmoniques par certaines conditions aux limites: applications à l'hydrodynamique'', on 24 June 1935.<ref name="AC"/><ref name="Mac">{{MacTutor|id=Iacob|title=Caius Iacob}}</ref><ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=95965}}</ref>

His most important work was in the studies of classical hydrodynamics, fluid mechanics, mathematical analysis, and compressible-flow theory.

Iacob started his academic career in 1935 at [[Politehnica University of Timișoara]], after which he became a professor at the University of Bucharest and at [[Babeș-Bolyai University]] in [[Cluj-Napoca|Cluj]]. In 1955, he was elected a corresponding [[list of members of the Romanian Academy|member of the Romanian Academy]], becoming a titular member in 1963.<ref name="Academiaromana.ro_2022-09-06">{{Citation | url=https://academiaromana.ro/bdar/armembriLit.php?vidT=I| title=Academia Română - membrii Academiei din 1866 până în prezent| newspaper=Academiaromana.ro| language=Romanian| accessdate=September 6, 2022}}</ref> From 1980 to the end of his life he served as President of the Mathematics section of the [[Romanian Academy]].<ref name="AC"/><ref name="Mac"/>

He was awarded several prizes for his work: the Henri de Parville Prize by the [[French Academy of Sciences]] (1940),<ref name="AC"/><ref name="Mac"/> the {{ill|State Prize of the Romanian People's Republic|ro|Premiul de Stat al Republicii Populare Române}} (1952),<ref name="AC"/> and the [[Order of the Star of the Romanian Socialist Republic|Order of the Star of the Romanian People's Republic]], 3rd class (1964).<ref>{{Citation | url=https://lege5.ro/Gratuit/g43dknrw/alegeconsolidare| title=Decretul nr. 635/1964 pentru conferirea titlului de Profesor Emerit al Republicii Populare Romîne, de ordine și medalii unor cadre didactice și tehnice-administrative de la Universitatea din București |website=lege5.ro| date=25 October 1964 | publisher= [[Monitorul Oficial]]| access-date=30 December 2021}}</ref>

In May 1990, he was [[1990 Romanian general election|elected]] [[Senate of Romania|senator]] for the [[Christian Democratic National Peasants' Party]] — the only member of the party to be elected to the upper chamber of the [[Parliament of Romania]] that year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.liceulcfrarad.ro/Doc/Caius%20Iacob.pdf|title=Caius Iacob| language=ro| website=www.liceulcfrarad.ro| access-date=30 December 2021}}</ref> He died in Bucharest in February 1992.<ref name="AC"/><ref name="Mac"/>

==Legacy==
Iacob was one of the founders of the Institute of Applied Mathematics of the [[Romanian Academy]] in 1991. Ten years later, the institute merged with the Center for Mathematical Statistics of the academy (that had been founded by [[Gheorghe Mihoc]] in 1964), becoming the current Gheorghe Mihoc–Caius Iacob Institute of Mathematical Statistics and Applied Mathematics of the Romanian Academy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ismma.ro/?page_id=228|title="Gheorghe Mihoc – Caius Iacob" Institute of Mathematical Statistics and Applied Mathematics of the Romanian Academy: History|website=ismma.ro|access-date=30 December 2021}}</ref>

A high school<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.liceulcfrarad.ro|title=Liceul tehnologic de electronică și automatizări Caius Iacob Arad| language=ro| website=www.liceulcfrarad.ro| access-date=30 December 2021}}</ref> and a middle school,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sgciar.ro|title=Școala Gimnazială Caius Iacob Arad| language=ro|website=sgciar.ro|access-date=30 December 2021}}</ref> as well as a street and a plaza{{Citation needed|date=August 2024}} in Arad also bear his name.
